# Anthony Calise

> Personal site of Anthony Calise — independent iOS app developer building focused, free, no-account apps for app blocking / screen-time (FightMode), fiber tracking, testosterone optimization, word puzzles, introvert confidence-building, and renter deposit protection. Each app pairs with a deeply researched blog covering the topic from a practical, science-backed angle.

This file is a curated map of acalise.com for AI search engines and language models. It points to the canonical pages for each topic the site covers and the most reliable sources for citations.

## Apps

- [FightMode: Boxing App Blocker](https://acalise.com/fightmode/) — App blocker for iPhone that makes you earn screen time. Block your chosen apps with Apple Screen Time; to open them, win a 60-second boxing or kickboxing round while a coach calls real combos, then get an AI scorecard on your technique. The first app blocker built for fighters; a boxing alternative to pushup blockers like Pushscroll. Free to download.
- [CloserLab: AI Sales Coach](https://acalise.com/closerlab/) — Free AI sales roleplay app for iPhone. Practise cold calls, objections and discovery against an AI buyer built from your actual offer, in voice or text, with a coaching score after each call. Built for individual reps rather than enablement teams.
- [ChartCheck: AI Chart Analysis](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/) — AI chart analysis app for iPhone. Screenshot any trading chart - stocks, crypto, forex, futures, ETFs - and get a structured technical read: trend and market structure, support and resistance zones, chart and candlestick patterns, visible indicator readings, a plain-language summary, a confidence level describing how legible the chart was, and an explicit "what I could not see" list. Educational tool; explicitly not financial advice and it does not recommend buying or selling anything.
- [Coach Dink: AI Pickleball Coach](https://acalise.com/coachdink/) — AI pickleball coach for iPhone. Film a game from a corner of the court and get a coaching report: a game score, the habits costing you points and why, ranked drills to fix them (50 drills: solo, partner or ball machine), doubles team reports, Match IQ lessons, and a rating estimate that updates after every filmed game. The rating is the app's own estimate, not an official rating.
- [FiberUp](https://acalise.com/fiberup/) — Free dedicated fiber tracker app for iPhone. USDA-verified fiber data, barcode scanner, daily progress ring, weekly plant count tracking. No account required.
- [T-Score](https://acalise.com/tscore/) — Free natural testosterone optimization tracker for iPhone. Tracks sleep, training, sunlight, cold exposure, and nutrition habits scientifically tied to testosterone.
- [Word Walk](https://acalise.com/word-walk/) — Free daily word ladder puzzle game for iPhone. Hand-crafted daily Lewis Carroll-style word ladders, vocabulary training, no ads.
- [Introvert: Daily Courage](https://acalise.com/introvert/) — Free social courage and confidence-building app for introverts. Daily small social challenges to grow comfort with everyday interactions.
- [MenuPics: Instant Picture Menu](https://acalise.com/menupics/) — Free AI menu scanner for iPhone. Snap any text-only restaurant menu and instantly see realistic photos of every dish. Works on foreign-language menus, QR-code PDFs, and chalkboards. No account required. Built on GCP / Cloud Run with Firebase App Check.

## Cold Calling & Sales Practice (CloserLab blog)

- [The 7 Best Sales Roleplay Apps and AI Practice Tools](https://acalise.com/closerlab/blog/best-sales-roleplay-apps/) — Enterprise platforms, team coaching software and the tools an individual rep can actually use alone, compared.
- [Cold Call Anxiety: Why It Happens](https://acalise.com/closerlab/blog/cold-call-anxiety/) — Call reluctance is anticipatory: the dread peaks before dialling and drops once someone answers. What actually reduces it, and why "just make the calls" and "be more confident" do not.
- [How to Practice Cold Calling Alone](https://acalise.com/closerlab/blog/how-to-practice-cold-calling/) — Five solo practice methods ranked by how well each transfers to a live call, and why silent script reading builds recognition rather than the ability to produce words under pressure.
- [Practising Cold Calls With ChatGPT](https://acalise.com/closerlab/blog/practice-cold-calls-with-chatgpt/) — The prompt that stops a chatbot playing a cooperative prospect, how to get useful in-character feedback, and the four things typed roleplay cannot rehearse.
- [How to Get Better at Cold Calling](https://acalise.com/closerlab/blog/how-to-get-better-at-cold-calling/) — What moves the needle in order: list quality, saying why you are calling early, asking rather than pitching, reviewing recordings, and drilling your three worst objections.

## Pickleball Coaching & Video Analysis (Coach Dink blog)

- [Pickleball Video Analysis: Apps, Coaches, or Reviewing It Yourself](https://acalise.com/coachdink/blog/pickleball-video-analysis-app/) — The three ways to get pickleball video analysis, compared honestly: your own film review, a coach, and AI apps. What each one catches and misses.
- [How to Film Your Pickleball Games: Phone Position, Angle, and Setup](https://acalise.com/coachdink/blog/how-to-film-pickleball/) — Where to put your phone to film a pickleball game, which lens to use, how high to mount it, and the five mistakes that ruin a clip before you watch it.
- [Pickleball Rating Levels Explained: What 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0 and 5.0 Mean](https://acalise.com/coachdink/blog/pickleball-rating-levels-explained/) — What pickleball rating levels mean from 2.5 to 5.0: the skills that define each level, the real gap between 3.5 and 4.0, and how ratings are assigned.
- [Pickleball Self Rating Guide: 12 Honest Questions to Find Your Level](https://acalise.com/coachdink/blog/pickleball-self-rating-guide/) — How to rate yourself at pickleball honestly: twelve yes-or-no questions that place you between 2.5 and 4.5, and the biases that make players rate too high.
- [12 Beginner Pickleball Mistakes and How to Fix Each One](https://acalise.com/coachdink/blog/beginner-pickleball-mistakes/) — The twelve mistakes that keep new pickleball players stuck at 2.5 and 3.0, why each one costs points, and a simple fix or drill for every one of them.
- [How to Improve at Pickleball When You Feel Stuck](https://acalise.com/coachdink/blog/how-to-improve-at-pickleball/) — More open play rarely breaks a pickleball plateau. The four-step loop that does: film a game, find two habits, drill them, then film again to check.
- [Pickleball Film Review: How to Watch Your Own Games and What to Look For](https://acalise.com/coachdink/blog/pickleball-film-review/) — How to review video of your own pickleball games: a three-pass checklist for position, shot choice and teamwork, what to ignore, and how to practise it.
- [The Best Pickleball Drills for 3.0, 3.5 and 4.0 Players](https://acalise.com/coachdink/blog/pickleball-drills-by-level/) — Pickleball drills matched to your level: what 3.0, 3.5 and 4.0 players should practise, how to run each drill with a partner, and how to know when to move up.
- [How to Hit a Third Shot Drop (and When to Drive Instead)](https://acalise.com/coachdink/blog/third-shot-drop/) — How to hit a pickleball third shot drop: the target, the swing, the footwork after it, when to drive instead, and the bounce rule that confuses everyone.
- [How to Dink in Pickleball: Technique, Targets and Patience](https://acalise.com/coachdink/blog/pickleball-dinking-tips/) — How to dink in pickleball: the stance, the stroke, where to aim, when to speed up, and when a lob beats a dink. Plus the patience habit most players lack.
- [The Pickleball Reset Shot: How and When to Hit It](https://acalise.com/coachdink/blog/pickleball-reset-shot/) — How to hit a pickleball reset: absorbing pace, landing it in the kitchen, and how a reset differs from a drop. Plus the transition-zone habits behind it.
- [How to Serve Better in Pickleball: Technique, Rules and Faults](https://acalise.com/coachdink/blog/pickleball-serve-tips/) — How to serve better in pickleball: a reliable deep serve, the volley and drop serve rules, foot faults, and whether a serve on the kitchen line is in or out.
- [Pickleball Kitchen Rules (Non-Volley Zone) and How to Use the Line](https://acalise.com/coachdink/blog/pickleball-kitchen-rules/) — The pickleball kitchen rules explained: what you can and cannot do in the non-volley zone, the momentum rule, and how to play from the kitchen line.
- [Pickleball Doubles Strategy: Positioning, Movement and Communication](https://acalise.com/coachdink/blog/pickleball-doubles-strategy/) — Pickleball doubles strategy that works at club level: where to stand on serve and return, moving as a pair, covering the middle, and what to say to your partner.
- [Pickleball Stacking Explained: How to Stack, and When It Is Worth It](https://acalise.com/coachdink/blog/pickleball-stacking/) — Pickleball stacking explained: why teams stack, the rules that make it legal, how to stack when serving and receiving, and the signals that keep it straight.

## AI Chart Analysis & Technical Analysis (ChartCheck blog)

- [AI Chart Analysis: What It Actually Does, and What It Can't](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/ai-chart-analysis/) — How a vision model reads a chart image, what it reliably identifies (structure, tested levels, named patterns, visible indicators), and the four things it structurally cannot know: anything outside the frame, order flow, fundamentals, and the future.
- [Using ChatGPT for Chart Analysis](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/chart-analysis-with-chatgpt/) — The five specific ways general-purpose chatbots fail on trading charts, including inventing precise price levels interpolated from axis labels, plus a prompt structure that fixes most of them.
- [How to Screenshot a Trading Chart So AI Can Read It](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/screenshot-a-chart-for-analysis/) — The seven things that must stay in frame, why 100-200 candles is the practical range, and the capture mistakes that produce confidently wrong analysis.
- [When AI Chart Analysis Gets It Wrong](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/why-ai-chart-analysis-is-wrong/) — Six recognisable failure modes and how to catch each one, including why a confidence score measures chart legibility rather than the probability a trade works.
- [AI Chart Analysis for Crypto](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/ai-chart-analysis-crypto/) — What a 24/7 market does to classical technical analysis: no gaps, noisier single-candle wick signals, exchange-specific volume, and levels that differ between venues.
- [AI Chart Analysis for Forex](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/ai-chart-analysis-forex/) — No consolidated volume (tick volume only), session structure that is invisible in a screenshot, and why currency pairs move for reasons on both sides.
- [Candlestick Patterns Explained](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/candlestick-patterns-explained/) — Body size, wick length and body position read most candles without memorising names; why location decides whether any pattern is meaningful.
- [Chart Patterns Cheat Sheet](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/chart-patterns-cheat-sheet/) — Continuation and reversal patterns grouped by what they say about supply and demand, with each pattern's invalidation level.
- [How to Read a Stock Chart](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/how-to-read-a-stock-chart/) — A beginner walkthrough in a fixed order: axes and timeframe, trend, structure, levels, then patterns and indicators last.
- [How to Draw Support and Resistance](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/support-and-resistance/) — Zones rather than lines, which levels are worth marking, why repeated tests can weaken a level, and how to tell a real break from a false one.
- [The Best AI Chart Analysis Apps, Grouped by What They Actually Do](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/best-ai-chart-analysis-apps/) — An honest guide to AI chart analysis apps: chatbots with vision, charting platforms with automated pattern tools, and dedicated screenshot analysers.
- [Free AI Chart Analysis: What You Actually Get, and the Hidden Costs](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/ai-chart-analysis-free/) — The genuinely free ways to get AI chart analysis, what each one does well, the hidden costs of free tools, and the red flags that mean free is a funnel.
- [AI Stock Analysis Prompts: Six Copy-Paste Templates That Avoid the Usual Traps](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/ai-stock-analysis-prompt/) — Six copy-paste prompts for AI stock chart analysis in ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini: first read, levels, patterns, timeframes, devil's advocate and journaling.
- [AI Technical Analysis of Stocks: What It Reads, and What Stocks Add](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/ai-technical-analysis-stocks/) — How AI technical analysis works on stock charts, the stock-specific details that change the read (gaps, earnings, volume, splits), and how to use it well.
- [AI Chart Analysis for Gold (XAUUSD): What Changes When the Chart Is Gold](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/ai-chart-analysis-gold/) — How to get a useful AI read of a gold chart: spot XAUUSD vs futures, tick volume, round-number levels, news spikes and the dollar link the chart cannot show.
- [Do AI Trading Bots Work? An Honest Look at What They Are and What They Promise](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/ai-trading-bots-explained/) — What AI trading bots actually do, why backtests mislead, the red flags in bot marketing, and how a bot differs from AI chart analysis that only describes.
- [Multi-Timeframe Analysis: How to Pick Your Timeframes and Read Them Together](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/multi-timeframe-analysis/) — How multi-timeframe analysis works, how to choose a set of timeframes for day trading or swing trading, and how to resolve conflicts between them.
- [How to Read Volume on a Stock Chart: Volume Analysis for Beginners](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/volume-analysis-trading/) — A practical guide to volume analysis: reading volume bars, breakouts, climaxes and dry-ups, relative volume, OBV and volume profile, and where volume misleads.
- [The RSI Indicator Explained: How to Read It Without Fooling Yourself](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/rsi-indicator-explained/) — How to read the RSI indicator: what the number measures, why 70 and 30 are not sell and buy signals, how RSI divergence works, and where it misleads you.
- [MACD Explained: How to Read the Lines, the Histogram and the Crossovers](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/macd-indicator-explained/) — How to read MACD: what the two lines and the histogram actually calculate, why crossovers lag, what the zero line tells you, and where MACD misleads.
- [How to Draw Fibonacci Retracement, and What the Levels Can and Cannot Tell You](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/fibonacci-retracement/) — How to draw Fibonacci retracement: choosing the swing, which way to drag, what 38.2, 50 and 61.8 mean, and why levels only matter with confluence.
- [How to Draw Trend Lines That Mean Something](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/how-to-draw-trend-lines/) — How to draw trend lines correctly: which points to connect, wicks versus bodies, why log scale changes everything, and how to tell a real break from noise.
- [The Head and Shoulders Pattern, and the Inverse Version, Explained](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/head-and-shoulders-pattern/) — How to spot a head and shoulders pattern and its inverse, where to draw the neckline, what confirms it, and why people see it everywhere.
- [The Bull Flag Pattern, the Bear Flag, and How Flags Differ From Pennants](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/bull-flag-pattern/) — How to spot a bull flag and a bear flag, what separates a flag from a pennant, what a valid flagpole looks like, and the signs a flag is actually failing.
- [Double Top and Double Bottom Patterns: How to Read Them Properly](https://acalise.com/chartcheck/blog/double-top-double-bottom/) — How to identify a double top and double bottom, why the middle swing is the line that matters, what confirms it, and how it differs from a range.

- [The Best Pushscroll Alternative in 2026](https://acalise.com/fightmode/blog/pushscroll-alternative/) — Alternatives to Pushscroll's pushup-to-unlock model: Repscroll, FitBlok, EarnScroll, and FightMode's boxing rounds.
